page: Amazon Web Services r9g.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 9th-generation AWS Graviton arm64 processor architecture. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated physical cores running at a fixed frequency of 3.3 GHz. Each core supports a single execution thread, eliminating hyperthreading-induced resource contention and offering predictable processing behavior. Memory capacity stands at 32.0 GB, which establishes a generous 1:8 compute-to-memory ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are present on this server configuration.

Regarding connectivity and storage, r9g.xlarge features a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage, meaning that all persistent disk storage must be provisioned via external, network-attached block storage volumes. While this design decouples storage scaling from compute resources, it introduces network dependencies for disk I/O latency and throughput. Additionally, the instance is deployed without complimentary public IPv4 addressing, requiring virtual private cloud networking configurations or Elastic IPs for external ingress.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the dedicated arm64 physical cores paired with 32.0 GB of RAM provide high memory density. This profile allows organizations to run memory-bound applications without paying for excess compute cores. The architecture suits workloads such as mid-sized relational databases, in-memory caching platforms like Redis and Memcached, analytics pipelines, continuous integration nodes with large memory footprints, and real-time data streaming engines.
description: Amazon Web Services r9g.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by AWS Graviton processors built on the arm64 architecture. Delivered via the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores operating at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz with a single thread per core, avoiding virtual thread contention. It offers 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a high 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance includes no local storage, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Graphical accelerators are omitted. Operating on dedicated ARM cores, r9g.xlarge delivers predictable compute isolation and high memory capacity per resource unit, translating to high efficiency for workloads constrained by RAM rather than raw compute scale. The configuration is suited for in-memory databases, Redis or Memcached caching tiers, memory-intensive data ingestion, and mid-sized transactional databases requiring stable memory density.
